_note: THE get_battle_status REPLY (not a push frame), captured verbatim by the operator on 2026-08-08 at 18:01:38, craftsman-1 (a50924913cef881c5e4d14257589d9ba) engaged with a Hollow Pilgrim at gold_run. This is the payload the executor's poll loop actually receives. Every earlier zone capture was a battle_started/battle_update PUSH; this one answers what those could not.
_what_this_settles: CONFIRMED, finding I1: there is NO `action` key in this reply. The client writes the raw `battle_status` key only from an action switch, so that key is NEVER populated for this command. GetRawJSON("battle_status") returns empty in production. This is no longer a suspicion — the shape-based fallback is mandatory, not defensive.
`combat_state` is an entirely UNMODELLED block. No serverapi struct covers it. It carries the real range mechanic.

`max_weapon_reach: 3` and per-participant `zone_distance: 6`. Range is NUMERIC. In-range is zone_distance <= max_weapon_reach, i.e. 6 must be closed to 3. The zone string (outer/inner) is a label over this number, not the primary signal.

`flee_counter: 0` with `flee_required: 3`. Fleeing takes THREE counts to complete. This quantifies review finding C1d.3 — the current code issues a flee stance and immediately returns, abandoning the ship mid-escape.
`can_escape: true` — whether escape is possible at all is server-reported, not assumed.

`is_npc: true` and `kind: "creature"` ARE present on this reply. This RESOLVES the review's open question and the spec's correction note: the wire carries both; it is the Go struct that lacks them. The spec's original claim was right about the wire and wrong only about reachability.
`auto_pilot` is PER-PARTICIPANT and is true on our own ship here while false on the creature. It is our ship's state, not a battle-wide flag.
The creature's `ship_name` is "grazer" — the role — while `username` is the display name "Hollow Pilgrim". Role is therefore visible in the battle payload too, not only in get_nearby.
EW state is exposed: em_disrupted, warp_disrupted, webbed, effective_speed. All false/1 here.
_still_open: Whether zone_distance closes by a fixed amount per advance, or scales with effective_speed. effective_speed is 1 here; no capture yet at another speed.
Whether max_weapon_reach varies by fitted weapon. 3 here with a Prospect and a pulse laser; treat it as read-from-the-wire, never hardcoded.
Whether a fleeing quarry increases zone_distance faster than one advance closes it — the practical question behind the give-up rule.
